description.description_long: On January 28, 2025, President Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14187, “Protecting Children From Chemical and Surgical Mutilation.” The order set a federal policy against funding, sponsoring, promoting, assisting, or supporting specified gender-transition procedures for people under 19 and directed executive agencies to take related steps involving grants, health programs, insurance, and TRICARE. Section 8(c) directs DOJ to investigate potential consumer deception, fraud, and Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act violations by entities discussing long-term effects of these procedures. Section 8(e) directs the Attorney General to prioritize investigations and take appropriate action against practices the order calls “child-abusive” by “sanctuary States” that facilitate stripping custody from parents who support their children’s healthy development. This is a federal policy directive with an express parental-custody component. The cited order does not itself document a parent’s prosecution, a criminal penalty imposed on parents for support, or an actual custody removal; those broader claims are omitted.
description.description_medium: On Jan. 28, 2025, Trump signed EO 14187, directing federal agencies to stop specified forms of federal support for gender-transition procedures for minors and to take related steps through grants, health programs, insurance, and TRICARE. It also directs DOJ to investigate providers and address state custody practices involving supportive parents. This documents an executive directive, not completed prosecutions of parents or actual custody removals.
description.description_short: Trump's Jan. 28 order directed limits on federal support for gender-transition care for minors and DOJ action on state custody practices affecting supportive parents.
